speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male. The patient has demonstrated inappropriate behavior, including making unfitting comments and attempts to kiss strangers, over the past 6 months. He shows disinterest in family interactions and has developed a particular craving for chocolate pudding and potato chips, resulting in a 10 kg weight gain. The patient also presents as unkempt.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cushing's Syndrome (likely due to an ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma or adrenal tumor).

The combination of weight gain, craving high-sugar/high-fat foods (pudding, chips), behavioral changes (inappropriate social conduct, unkempt appearance), and potential fluid retention strongly suggests hypercortisolism. I recommend a 24-hour urinary free cortisol test and a plasma ACTH level to confirm the diagnosis and localize the source.

REQUEST TEST: 24-hour urinary free cortisol
REQUEST TEST: Plasma ACTH level

Do you have any history of hypertension, muscle weakness, or easy bruising?
